identity.title: Disruption of BnPHT5;1a reduces arsenic accumulation through Pi-dependent restriction of arsenate uptake in Brassica napus.

content.abstract: Arsenic (As) contamination threatens crop production and food safety, yet the role of vacuolar Pi transporters in arsenate [As(V)] acquisition remains unclear in polyploid crops. Here, we investigated BnPHT5;1a, a vacuolar Pi influx transporter in Brassica napus. Double mutants of the two B. napus homeologs BnA09PHT5;1a and BnC09PHT5;1a (BnPHT5;1a DM), generated by simultaneous CRISPR/Cas9 editing, exhibited enhanced As(V) tolerance. Under 400 muM As(V), mutant shoot and root fresh weights were 11.0-30.1% higher and root As concentrations were approximately 28% lower than those of wild-type W10. Heterologous overexpression increased As(V) sensitivity in Arabidopsis. Yeast growth assays provided no clear evidence of direct As(V) transport by BnPHT5;1a. Its disruption reduced the expression of several plasma membrane PHT1 genes and limited As(V) uptake under Pi-sufficient conditions, with these effects diminishing as external Pi availability decreased. Mutant plants displayed an attenuated transcriptional response to As(V), consistent with a lower As burden. These findings support an As(V)-avoidance mechanism in BnPHT5;1a DM and suggest possible functional differences between BnPHT5;1a and BnPHT5;1b, whose disruption was previously associated with increased As accumulation and shoot cell wall retention. This study highlights the role of vacuolar Pi partitioning in As(V) acquisition and provides a potential genetic target for breeding low-As rapeseed.
